claims.statement: For binary logistic occupancy observations with Gaussian N(0,I) prior, one positive and one negative outcome at each design row b_j yield V(z)=0.5||z||^2+2 sum_j log cosh(b_j^T z/2) up to a constant, with supplied minimizer z=0 and Hessian I+0.5 B^T diag(sech^2(Bz/2)) B. If B^T B<=2I, then I<=Hessian<=2I globally; the sparse coupled B=[I;C/2] with rows of C equal to e_k+e_(k+1) satisfies this for every d because ||C||<=2.
assumptions: independent binary equilibrium-occupancy observations with logistic response in standardized log-affinity coordinates
Gaussian prior N(0,I)
balanced positive/negative pair at every calibrated design row
exact value-gradient oracle and supplied minimizer as required by family 139
claims.status: internally derived exact model fit to a source-reported oracle theorem; no experiment or independent source-proof audit
claims.novelty_boundary: The logistic Hessian and oracle premise are standard; this is a concrete model-interface construction, not a new sampling theorem. Balanced outcomes have prior-predictive probability at most 2^(-(2d-1)), and the theorem gives oracle-query rather than bit-time or assay-sample bounds.

costs.assays: 4d-2 binary observations for 2d-1 paired design rows
costs.matrix_storage: O(d) nonzero design entries for the stated sparse B
costs.oracle: C_epsilon*d^epsilon exact value-gradient calls for fixed epsilon under the source theorem; unrestricted computation is uncharged

claims.falsifier: An algebraic error in the paired logistic likelihood or a design matrix violating B^T B<=2I; experimentally, failure of the calibrated response to follow the stated logistic model.
claims.next_gate: Find a non-rare biological dataset with known MAP and global Hessian condition number at most 2, then independently audit the source sampler and charge data/bit costs.

claims.statement: If independent table entries X_gc are geometric on nonnegative integers with odds rho_gc=a_g b_c<1, then conditioning on all row and column sums makes the table uniform on its fixed-margin fiber. Therefore an exact uniform sampler for the unrestricted fiber supports a conditionally exact Monte Carlo rank test for a prespecified statistic.
assumptions: independent geometric entries with odds rho_gc=a_g b_c
all cells have unbounded nonnegative support and no structural zeros/caps
condition on exact observed row and column margins
test statistic and tail direction prespecified, or selection accounted for
source exact sampler is used; it has expected-polynomial rather than every-run polynomial bit time
claims.status: conditional model bridge internally derived; sampler theorem source-reported and unverified
claims.novelty_boundary: The factorization identity and exchangeability p-value are standard. Application is specific to geometric/NB-shape-1 counts; Poisson and NB-shape-2 conditional laws are not uniform. Structural-zero/capped counting is a separate FPRAS result, not the exact sampler.

costs.data: one observed gene-by-cell count table and exact margins
costs.sampling: M independent exact tables at M times expected-polynomial bit cost

claims.falsifier: A nonconstant joint probability over the fixed-margin fiber under the stated independent-geometric factorized-odds model, or violation of the exchangeability assumptions.
claims.next_gate: Validate the geometric separable-odds null on a named count assay and externally review the exact sampler proof.

claims.statement: Under a null that fixes labeled compartments and degree sequences and independently draws a uniform graph realization within each compartment, a prespecified plus-one Monte Carlo rank test for a graph statistic is conditionally super-uniform. Family 131 supplies a source-reported polynomial-mixing switch chain for every graphical labeled degree sequence; its exact uniform sampler is almost-surely terminating in expected polynomial bit time with an exponential-enumeration branch.
assumptions: labeled vertices and their degree sequence are fixed
each stratum has complete-host simple-graph support matching the family 131 theorem
observed graph is exchangeable with independent null draws conditional on the fixed summaries
statistic and tail direction are prespecified or selection-adjusted
claims.status: conditional statistical application; source theorem unverified; no new network-science theorem
claims.novelty_boundary: Degree-conditioned network randomization is established practice. This maps the exact source interface to a finite test and preserves geometry/compartment confounding as an explicit failure boundary.

costs.mixing: source claim: TV<=1/4 within 2n^8 steps for its specified lazy switch chain
costs.exact_sampling: expected-polynomial bit time, not every-run polynomial time
costs.Monte_Carlo: B>=log(2/beta)/(2*epsilon^2) for tail-probability accuracy epsilon at failure beta

claims.falsifier: A violation of exchangeability after conditioning on the labeled degrees/strata, including unmodeled geometry that changes the graph law.
claims.next_gate: Compare against a compartment- and distance-preserving null and verify source theorem/sampler behavior.

claims.statement: For any finite rational d-by-d matrix tuple A_i, let m=d+1, E=[e_1-e_m,...,e_d-e_m], F=[I_d 0]-(1/m)1_d1_m^T, J=11^T/m. For c=1/2 and sufficiently small rational t>0, P_i=J+E(cI+tA_i)F are strictly positive doubly stochastic kernels similar to diag(1,cI+tA_i), and A_i=t^-1(FP_iE-cI). For Phi=s_4(X_1,...,X_4)(I+X_5)^-1, a nonzero source hit remains nonzero after this common stochastic embedding, while the readout can be as small as order t^4.
assumptions: all source matrices have the same finite dimension and exact rational entries
t is selected small enough for entrywise positivity and invertibility
s_4 is the alternating standard degree-four polynomial and scalar identity insertions cancel
readout observes enough transition outcomes to estimate each kernel
claims.status: internally derived representation lemma; source hit list and proof remain source-reported; physical sample-margin usefulness unresolved
claims.novelty_boundary: This removes the 2-state standard-polynomial obstruction at the level of representation; similar embeddings may be standard and priority is unknown. The source gives no polynomial physical signal margin, manageable hitting-list search, or end-to-end experiment protocol.

costs.channel_calibration: transition tomography for each kernel, each starting state, and each output state
costs.signal: proportional to t^4 times source polynomial separation
costs.shot_cost: order gamma^-2 observations per transition probability to resolve signal gamma; may be exponential in source entry bit height

claims.falsifier: A failure of exact simultaneous similarity or an example where the transformed rational formula vanishes despite a nonzero source evaluation and invertible denominator.
claims.next_gate: Audit actual source tuple height/list-size bounds, derive a lower bound on the smallest nonzero hit, and either prove polynomial readout cost or close the physical route.

claims.statement: For fixed deletion probability q, the family-122 source assertion n^A min_{x!=y}TV(D_q(x),D_q(y))->0 for every A implies that any polynomial number of iid complete deletion-only reads gives equal-prior recovery at most 1/2+o(1) for a minimizing binary tag pair, if that pair is in the codebook.
assumptions: two-base A/C tag encoding
fixed known iid per-position deletion probability
complete ordered traces, no position labels/flanks, no insertions/substitutions/dropouts
tag codebook contains the hard pair
claims.status: conditional cross-field implication internally derived from source-reported theorem; full proof unverified
claims.novelty_boundary: The source lower theorem is not new work here; high-rate coded trace recovery is known prior art. Full DNA storage-channel behavior is outside the deletion-only inner-code interface.

costs.samples: m reads per tag; the lower bound is independent of computation
costs.processing: at most mn observed bases per tag
costs.omitted: pool dropout, PCR bias, synthesis, indexing, sequence filters and non-deletion errors

claims.falsifier: The source hard-pair theorem/product-TV derivation fails, or the application codebook/channel violates stated premises.
claims.next_gate: Materialize source hard pairs and compare deletion-only software replay with a theorem-backed coded control; then measure platform deviations before any wet-lab inference.

overall_status: No OpenAI/math theorem proof was independently verified; no experiment was conducted; historical novelty remains unknown. Results are conditional interface constructions, model-specific capability paths, or scoped counterexamples.
